metrics.filter_note: No bulk-sync outlier this window (largest single commit was 2398 insertions) -- unlike the prior 3 retros, raw and filtered are identical.
metrics.focus_area: trm intake-triage-manifest feature (5-task cross-repo SDD build, trm + cic-ingestion) + TODOS.md backlog hygiene

session_focus.summary: Cross-repo feature build via full brainstorming -> plan -> subagent-driven-development pipeline: resumable pre-scan/triage manifest for TRM's raw file-dump ingest (trm repo, 4 tasks) plus a Vision-labels passthrough on the cic-ingestion image-analysis service it depends on (1 task). Design reused an existing but never-implemented extension point (classify.ts's aspect-ratio placeholder, explicitly documented as swap-in-ready) instead of building parallel plumbing. Final whole-branch review (opus, both repos) caught 2 Critical bugs neither per-task review nor the implementers' own green tests caught: resumability was inverted (failed files got silently marked permanently-done on next run) and dedup never actually flagged duplicates (isDup was always false). Both fixed and re-review-verified clean. Both branches merged locally and pushed.
incidents: 3 separate implementer subagents (of 5 total tasks) committed directly to the main trm/cic-ingestion checkouts instead of the isolated git worktree, despite explicit dispatch-prompt warnings after the first occurrence. All 3 caught before any push (verified via git log/status diff against the worktree branch), fixed via cherry-pick-onto-worktree + git revert-off-main (never reset --hard, never touched unrelated pre-existing uncommitted files in either checkout). No data lost, but this is now a 3-for-5 rate on this session's task dispatches -- the cwd-verification instruction in the prompt did not prevent it, worth investigating a structural fix (e.g. a pre-commit hook inside the worktree that refuses commits if cwd resolves outside .worktrees/) rather than relying on prompt text.

The final-review reviewer found a residual design flaw the fix wave correctly implemented-as-specified but couldn't fully resolve: intake-manifest.json is hash-keyed (one entry per content hash), so flagging a duplicate isDup:true overwrites the sole record for that hash -- a downstream `!isDup` filter (the design spec's own stated consumption pattern) would drop the content entirely rather than keep one canonical copy, and the canonical sourcePath gets overwritten by the latest-seen duplicate's path. Confirmed harmless today (no consumer reads isDup yet) but is a real blocker parked in TODOS.md for whoever builds the first downstream consumer.
process_learnings: Plan-embedded reference code is not exempt from scrutiny: all 3 of the final review's highest-severity findings (resumability inversion, dead dedup flag, one HEIC misclassification path) were present verbatim in the plan document's own example code, and every task-scoped review passed because each task's tests were also copied from the same plan -- the plan supplied both the bug and the test that failed to catch it. Task-scoped review verifies 'matches the brief'; only the broad final review, read with fresh eyes against the design intent rather than the brief's literal text, caught that the brief itself was wrong.

File-structure mapping during plan-writing (not just during implementation) is where real reuse opportunities surface: reading ingestDir.ts and classify.ts before finalizing the vision-classifier design revealed a documented, signature-stable placeholder built for exactly this purpose, cutting the plan from 'new endpoint + new module' to 'fill in an existing extension point' -- worth doing that file-structure read-through as a standing step before locking task boundaries, not just before writing task code.
